name: Pharisees The
overview: The Pharisees were a prominent Jewish sect known for their strict adherence to the law and ambition for precedence, yet Scripture reveals their hypocrisy and spiritual blindness. They rejected true repentance, as seen when John the Baptist called them a 'generation of vipers' for their insincere approach to baptism (Matthew 3:7). Jesus condemned their insufficient righteousness, warning that it must exceed theirs to enter the kingdom of heaven (Matthew 5:20), and criticized their association with sinners and their accusations against Him, such as claiming He cast out demons by demonic power (Matthew 9:11, 9:34; 12:24). Ultimately, the Pharisees' opposition to Christ was marked by cruelty and conspiracy to destroy Him (Matthew 12:14), highlighting their rejection of the gospel and true salvation.
